answer: A cloned roster cannot pre-fracture a coupon etched after check-in. The applicant escrows 9.05 POA and, at lab bench F, splits a provided shale coupon along a door-etched laser scribe, winds the dust into a 5-turn spiral vial, and locks it under a numbered bench anchor for 50 minutes while mass and grain stills stamp every 100 seconds. Reviewers recompute mass from the coupon's posted density and refuse a second vial from the same lot. Cost: 9.05 POA plus one live split. A pre-crushed coupon, mass drift above 3%, or a borrowed bench anchor slashes 52% and closes bench F for three epochs.
